Confirming irreversible actions (fixture guidance)
Ask for confirmation before an action that cannot be undone, and state the consequence in the dialog text, for example which package will be awarded and to whom.
Label the confirm button with the action itself, such as Award package, rather than a generic OK.
Do not ask for confirmation of actions that can be undone easily; offer undo instead.
This page is a test fixture for the Feature Research Agent and is not real documentation.

1	Dialog focus management (fixture guidance)
2	When a modal dialog opens, move keyboard focus to the first focusable element inside the dialog, or to the dialog heading when the first control is destructive.
3	While the dialog is open, keep focus within the dialog until it is dismissed.
4	When the dialog closes, return focus to the control that opened it; if that control no longer exists, move focus to a logical place such as the page heading.
5	This page is a test fixture for the Feature Research Agent and is not real documentation.

1	Preventing duplicate submissions (fixture guidance)
2	Disable the submit control after the first click and show progress, so a double click does not send the action twice.
3	On the server, treat repeated requests carrying the same idempotency key as one operation.
4	If a second attempt is made after the first succeeded, report the existing result instead of performing the action again.
